paper_title: On the Role of Model Prior in Real-World Inductive Reasoning
caption: Human pairwise comparison results on three datasets, showing preferences for hypotheses with, without demos, and cases where it was hard to tell the difference.
model_annotation: The image presents a set of three pie charts illustrating human pairwise comparison results across three datasets—labeled "Truthful Review," "Funny Reddit," and "Unhealthy Comments"—to compare preferences for hypotheses with or without demos. A shared legend at the top identifies the three categories represented in each chart: "W/o Demos" in gray, "Hard to Tell" in blue, and "W/ Demos" in light green. Each pie chart contains exactly three slices, with percentage labels displayed directly inside the segments, and none of the slices are exploded or otherwise visually emphasized. In the top "Truthful Review" chart, the gray "W/o Demos" slice is the largest at 43.0%, followed by the light green "W/ Demos" slice at 34.1%, and the blue "Hard to Tell" slice at 22.9%. The bottom-left "Funny Reddit" chart displays the gray "W/o Demos" slice at 41.5%, the light green "W/ Demos" slice at 37.1%, and the blue "Hard to Tell" slice at 21.5%. Similarly, the bottom-right "Unhealthy Comments" chart shows the gray "W/o Demos" slice at 37.8%, the light green "W/ Demos" slice at 34.8%, and the blue "Hard to Tell" slice at 27.4%. Visually, the spatial arrangement of the categories is fixed across all three charts, and the slices consistently appear in descending order of size from gray, to light green, and finally blue.
